results.title: Can Generative AI improve social science?
results.content: I argue Generative AI has the potential to improve survey research, online experiments, automated content analyses, agent-based models, and other techniques commonly used to study human behavior. These include experiments where human respondents interact with Generative AI, or simulations where researchers prompt models to interact with each other to study emergent group behaviors. By developing our own Generative AI models, social scientists can more effectively diagnose how the model training process impacts scientific analysis of human behavior and ensure these new tools evolve according to the interest of science, and not only the corporations that produce many of the most popular models at present. Regardless of whether Generative AI can effectively simulate human behavior, it may also help social scientists with other common research tasks such as content analysis of text-based data. Rather than guessing when and how proprietary models may exhibit bias—or endlessly testing different prompts to achieve research goals—social scientists could work together to identify the limitations of Generative AI tools for social science research.

results.title: Can ChatGPT enhance business student creativity? ...
results.content: This study examines the impact of generative AI (genAI) tools, specifically ChatGPT, on university student creativity across three disciplines: Marketing, Management, and Entrepreneurship. Thus, we aim to investigate the impact of generative AI (specifically ChatGPT) on the divergent thinking components of creativity among undergraduate students across three academic disciplines (Marketing, Management, and Entrepreneurship.). Recent studies are increasingly focusing on the role of AI in general and ChatGPT in particular in higher education, particularly its potential to support and enhance creativity in student learning and academic tasks (Cope, Kalantzis, and Searsmith Citation2021; Kasneci et al. We chose this as a means of evaluating the impact of ChatGPT-3.5 on student creativity across the three academic disciplines because it is a domain-independent test, simple to administer, easily adaptable, and broadly acceptable as an indicator of divergent thinking across disciplines and is in use in current research in assessing the effects of ChatGPT on creative output (Haase and Hanel Citation2023).
